summary: Beach Point light at the mouth of Pubnico Harbour, Nova Scotia: a family of Amiro keepers for about 80 years; fibreglass tower of 1984 still lit.

structures.note: Original tower; the Amiro family kept it; removed 1967 (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett). Construction date 1853 per LighthouseFriends; station 1854 per Rowlett.
Freestanding fibreglass tower at the end of the spit; Rowlett gives 11 m (36 ft), LighthouseFriends 11.5 m (38 ft)

access.note: Canadian Coast Guard property. Lighthouse Road, a 0.3 km gravel road off Route 3 north of Charlesville; no parking provided; grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett).

events.note: Finished in 1853; Maturin Amiro appointed first keeper (LighthouseFriends). Rowlett and the station record give 1854.

Ten-foot addition to the tower and an iron lantern room from Peggy's Point; sixth-order Fresnel lens (LighthouseFriends). The Department's 1909 report calls the light it replaced a seventh-order dioptric light (conflict).
Whistling buoy established 1 February 1901, 6 miles south-west by west of the harbour light
New lantern and fourth-order lens; occulting white, six seconds on and four off (LighthouseFriends dates 1908; the Department's 1909 report lists the change as an improvement)
Fire destroyed the lantern room on 19 January 1926; a fixed white light shown until repairs (LighthouseFriends)
Original lighthouse removed; light shown from a skeletal tower on a fog-alarm building (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett)
Freestanding fibreglass tower erected near the end of the spit (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett)
Light de-staffed 7 September 1987; last keeper Merle Thomas (LighthouseFriends)
Light and fog alarm deactivated (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett: inactive 2000 to 2005)

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1907 keeper table row (p. 143, scan 150) was read on the page image; the appointment date (6 February 1893) comes from that image, since the OCR keeps the columns apart. The 1901 buoy (p. 62, scan 77), 1902 tide gauge (p. 110, scan 123) and 1909 'Improvements' entry (p. 70, scan 77, 'Beach Point, Pubnico Harbour') are confirmed in the report text. Fog alarm wording corrected: LighthouseFriends says the light, not the fog alarm, was re-established in 2005; Rowlett says the light was inactive 2000 to 2005. Beach Point is a sandspit (Rowlett) and a low spit or beach (LighthouseFriends); the earlier 'gravel spit' was not in either source. The Amiro name is from LighthouseFriends; the Acadian Shores page says only 'three generations of the same family'. 1) Dates: LighthouseFriends says the lighthouse was finished in 1853 and the Acadian Shores site says the light has stood since 1853; Rowlett and the station record say the station was established in 1854. The story gives both and uses 1854 as first lit. 2) Spelling: LighthouseFriends writes Amiro. The Department's 1904 to 1908 keeper tables read 'Amero, Geo. D' (OCR; the 1912 and 1915 tables read 'G. D. Amiro'). Not conflated with W. H. Amiro, customs officer, who observed the 1902 tide gauge and is not a keeper. 3) Lens order: LighthouseFriends says a sixth-order Fresnel lens was used from 1889; the Department's 1909 report calls the fixed white light it replaced a seventh-order dioptric light. Both are cited and the story says the sources disagree. 4) Tower height of the 1984 fibreglass tower: Rowlett 11 m (36 ft); LighthouseFriends 11.5 m (38 ft); the station record 11.5 m. 5) The pre-1900 history (petition, Condon's 1857 visit, 1858 to 1889 works, 1890 to 1891 breakwater, 1898 foghorn, 1926 fire) rests on LighthouseFriends, which cites the Journal of the House of Assembly and Department reports not in the corpus. Each such sentence is footnoted to LighthouseFriends and says so. Condon's words are quoted second-hand. 6) Chronicling America: one search for Pubnico with 'lighthouse' failed (IncompleteRead on loc.gov, retry not completed); no wreck or storm report for the station was found, so the Storms chapter rests on LighthouseFriends alone. 7) Austin J. Amiro and Elmer Larkin are not checked in the Department lists (the corpus has no Amiro entries after 1916 for Pubnico). 8) The 1909 report line reads 'the flxed white, 7th order dioptric light' (OCR typo 'flxed' kept out of quotes). 9) The record's material 'wood' for the current tower is a correction: the 1984 tower is fibreglass.
